title: Runtime install failure autopsy and Terraform quirks
content:
Summary:
This is a working autopsy-style runbook for common install/runtime failures we've seen in VPC/on-prem deployments plus a set of Terraform module gotchas that repeatedly show up during upgrades. Intended audience: oncall engs, install SREs, field eng who run customer installs. Not a formal playbook yet — more of a grab-bag of high-signal heuristics, commands, and quick remediations.

Scope / When to use: 
- Use this when an installation fails during bootstrap, pods crash on first start, or a model runtime segfaults immediately after upgrade.
- Focus is infra/service-level issues (drivers, container runtime, cgroup, kernel ABI, TF drift) rather than app-level bugs in the model code.

Quick smoke checklist (10 minute triage):
- Can the host reach the registry and package repos? curl -fsS https://registry-... || check network ACLs
- Is GPU visible? nvidia-smi || lspci | grep -i nvidia
- Container runtime running? systemctl status docker || systemctl status containerd; crictl ps -a
- Check node resource limits: free -h; df -h; ulimit -n; sysctl vm.max_map_count
- Kernel/cgroups version: cat /proc/filesystems | grep cgroup; mount | grep cgroup
- Journal for first-failure timestamp: journalctl -u redwood-runtime -S "-1h" | sed -n '1,200p'
- TF plan drift: terraform plan -target=module.runtime -out=check.plan (compare with last apply)
- Look for OOM kill: dmesg | grep -i kill; journalctl -k | tail -n 200

Failure signatures, likely causes, quick checks, and fixes:
1) Immediate segfault or SIGILL in runtime binary at container start
   - Symptom: container exits with code 139/132; core dump saved; logs show illegal instruction.
   - Likely causes: binary built for a different CPU ISA (AVX2 vs AVX512), incompatible glibc/kernel ABI, or runtime compiled with unsupported instruction set.
   - Quick checks: file /opt/redwood/bin/runtime; lscpu | egrep 'Flags|Model name' ; readelf -A /opt/redwood/bin/runtime | grep Tag_ABI
   - Fix: deploy the CPU-compatible build (use -cpu-arch flag in salt/ansible/Terraform module), or pin runtime image tag that matches customer's CPU family. Add a preflight that checks /proc/cpuinfo for required flags.

2) Container stuck in CrashLoop backoff during first kv-cache warmup
   - Symptom: repeated restarts 30s apart; logs show memory allocation failure or permission denied while mmap.
   - Causes: insufficient RLIMIT, sysctl vm.max_map_count too low, no memlock privileges, seccomp profile blocking mmap/PROT flags, transparent hugepages causing fragmentation.
   - Checks: ulimit -l; sysctl vm.max_map_count; cat /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled; journalctl -u containerd | grep seccomp
   - Fix: increase limits in systemd unit or kube pod security context (resources.memory, securityContext.capabilities), disable THP or set to madvise, add memlock to limits.conf, relax seccomp for failing syscalls.

3) GPU visible but model process fails with CUDA driver errors at startup
   - Symptom: CUDA driver minor/major mismatch; errors like "GPU driver version < runtime required" or libnvidia-ml.so not found.
   - Checks: nvidia-smi; dpkg -l | grep nvidia; grep -i nvidia /var/log/syslog
   - Fix: ensure host driver matches container tooling: install nvidia-driver X, nvidia-container-toolkit version Y. For kube, verify node has the correct nvidia-device-plugin and node-labels. If host upgrade needed, schedule node drain.

4) Model runtime stalls after a few tokens / massive latency spike
   - Symptom: first requests succeed, subsequent requests very slow. Logs: long GC pauses, blocked threads on epoll, or high context switches.
   - Causes: thread affinity wrong, hugepage misconfig, swap enabled, CPU frequency scaling governor set to powersave, NUMA affinity wrong for GPU attachments.
   - Checks: top -H; perf top briefly; cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; numactl --hardware
   - Fix: set governor to performance, disable swap, enforce thread affinity in runtime config, use numactl binding for runtime processes, enable hugepages if workload benefits.

5) Networking blocked between control plane and nodes (VPC specific ACLs)
   - Symptom: bootstrap times out waiting for kv-store or control-plane healthcheck, TLS handshakes fail.
   - Checks: curl/control-plane health endpoint; tcpdump port 443 or custom port; check security group / firewall rules and VPC flow logs.
   - Fix: open required ports, update TF to create correct SG rules, document cross-account peering rules.

Terraform module notes / recurring gotchas:
- Provider version pinning: we had a recurring break when aws provider moved to 5.x and resource schemas changed. Always pin provider in root module: required_providers { aws = "~> 4.50" } for known-good stacks.
- Module variable defaults that trigger replacement: module runtime had size=="medium" default; change to null to avoid unintentional replacements on upgrade.
- State drift from manual node tagging: customers sometimes tag nodes outside TF; add lifecycle.ignore_changes for tags that customers may modify, or clearly document that tags are managed by TF.
- Terraform apply ordering + onprem (provisioners): avoid instance-level remote-exec that depends on image preboots — convert to cloud-init or external provisioner to reduce bootstrap flakiness.
- Plan readability: use terraform plan -detailed-exitcode and save plan JSON for automated drift analysis in CI.
- Sensitive defaults: do not expose long-lived SSH keys in modules; use keypair resource referencing customer KMS-managed keys.

Upgrade plan checklist (preflight, canary, rollback hooks):
- Pre-upgrade: capture current images / versions (kubectl get pods -n redwood -o custom-columns=..), export logs for last 24h, baseline perf SLOs and token cost metrics.
- Canary: pick 1 node pool (or 1 on-prem rack) with non-critical workload, run tf apply with create_before_destroy where possible, watch for resource eviction, watch metric series for latency regressions.
- Health gates: no pod restarts > 0 in 10 minutes, 99th latency < baseline *1.5, no new OOM events, model inference success rate > 99%.
- Rollback: keep last-known-good TF state snapshot and terraform state backup; have image tags pinned in var image_tag_previous. Automated rollback should run terraform apply with previous plan file if gates fail.

Recovery play examples (snippets):
- Force recreate runtime on a single node: kubectl cordon node-1; kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data; terraform taint module.runtime.kubernetes_deployment.runtime[0]; terraform apply -target=module.runtime -auto-approve
- Collect for postmortem: tar logs script: /usr/local/bin/collect-runtime-diagnostics.sh --since 24h --output /tmp/cust-12345-diagnostics.tar.gz

Debug commands cheat-sheet (most useful):
- journalctl -u redwood-runtime -b --no-pager | tail -n 200
- crictl ps -a; crictl logs <id>
- docker inspect <container> | jq '.HostConfig'
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.used --format=csv
- sudo sysctl -a | egrep 'vm.max_map_count|vm.overcommit_memory|fs.file-max'
- lsof -p <pid> | wc -l (file descriptor usage)

Notes / open items (TODOs):
- Add CPU feature preflight to installer: detect AVX/AVX2/AVX512 and fail fast with clear message.
- Add automatic driver compatibility check in TF module (or hook that checks host nvidia driver before installing container).
- Add CI test that applies module against a small emulated TF state that simulates node tags changed outside TF (catch lifecycle.ignore_changes regressions).
- Decide on default policy for transparent hugepages in our docs (madvise vs never).

References and links:
- Confluence: /team-private-deploys/runtime-install-guidance (linked above)
- GitHub PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR-987 (tf provider pin), github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/402 (secure-cgroup-v2 support)
- JIRA tickets: INF-2378 (customer-a install failure), INF-2411 (driver-mismatch during upgrade)

Quick follow-ups for next pass (for product and infra):
- Product: capture a simple telemetry event when a runtime binary fails ABI checks to aggregate frequency of CPU mismatch.
- Infra: provide a helper binary that validates host prerequisites (driver, cgroups, sysctl) and returns machine-readable JSON for installer and TF.

Footer: remember this is a draft/working notebook. If you add a step that stabilizes a customer install, move it to the canonical 'onprem-deploy-healthcheck-and-fallback-procedures' doc and add a short changelog here.
